title: The reclaim failed; leverage is now the pressure point
dek: Coinbase price structure, Farside ETF flows, OKX open interest, and the U.S. 10-year yield through 7 October 2026.
thesis: The $86k reclaim failed. BTC is testing $82–83k intraday while open interest is 9.4% higher than a week ago.
stakes: The current move is a long-led forced unwind, not yet a synchronized cross-market panic. A completed UTC close below $82k would confirm the next door.
subscribeHook: A completed close below $82k — or a clean reclaim of $86k — updates the sequence. Charts stay free here; the call moves by email.
sourceNote: Coinbase Exchange BTC-USD daily UTC candles through the partial 7 October session; Farside Investors US-session ETF flows through 6 October; OKX public BTC aggregate open-interest observations through 7 October 16:00 UTC; U.S. 10-year yield from FRED through 5 October; CoinMarketCap liquidation snapshot and Emily cross-market snapshot at 18:29 UTC. The 7 October candle is partial and the Farside row is incomplete; blanks are not zeroes. Educational scenario research; no leverage.

briefs.headline: $82–83k is being tested, not yet lost
briefs.lede: 6 October reached $86,698 but closed at $85,540. The partial 7 October candle is near $83,261 after touching $82,717.
briefs.bodyHtml:
Fact. The only completed close above $86k was 4 October. The next two completed sessions closed back below it. At 18:40 UTC on 7 October, BTC was down about 2.7% from the prior close, but the daily candle was still open.

Read. The reclaim failed and the first support door is under pressure. A wick into $82–83k is not the same as a completed close below $82k.

Decision rule. A completed UTC close below $82k opens $80k, then $77k. Acceptance back above $86k would invalidate the immediate breakdown path.

briefs.headline: ETF demand flipped back to green, but not with breakout force
briefs.lede: Farside recorded −$89.8M on 5 October and +$118.8M on 6 October: a two-session net of only +$29.0M.
briefs.bodyHtml:
Fact. The 6 October inflow reversed the prior day's outflow, but it remained far below the +$999.0M impulse on 21 September. The 7 October row was incomplete at retrieval and is shown as missing, not zero.

Read. ETF demand is mixed and modest. It neither confirms a durable cash bid nor proves distribution by itself.

Watch. Repeated outflows alongside a completed break below $82k would strengthen the downside case. Strong inflows with a reclaim of $86k would weaken it.

briefs.headline: Leverage rebuilt faster than price
briefs.lede: OKX aggregate BTC open interest rose from $3.06B on 30 September to $3.34B on 7 October, while BTC was roughly flat over that span before today's partial selloff.
briefs.bodyHtml:
Fact. OKX open interest is up about 9.4% in seven days and average recent BTC-USDT perpetual funding is still positive at roughly 0.0035% per eight hours. CoinMarketCap's 18:29 UTC snapshot showed about $954M of 24-hour crypto liquidations, approximately 94% longs; BTC accounted for about $409M.

Read. This is the clearest active stress signal: a crowded long unwind can accelerate a support break. It is not, by itself, evidence of market-wide panic.

Watch. Falling price with stubborn or rising open interest is the dangerous combination. Falling open interest with support holding would indicate leverage is clearing.

briefs.headline: Rates are hostile; the rest of the market is not in panic
briefs.lede: The U.S. 10-year yield reached 5.31% on 5 October while Nasdaq and the S&P 500 remained near their 45-day highs.
briefs.bodyHtml:
Fact. FRED's latest 10-year yield observation was 5.31%, up 7 basis points over five observations. Emily's latest cross-market snapshot showed VIX at 15.01 and the U.S. high-yield spread at 3.03%, with neither signaling synchronized stress.

Read. High rates create valuation and liquidity vulnerability, but calm volatility and credit argue against calling this a broad panic. The current evidence fits a crypto-led leverage event.

Wildcard. Reprice quickly if volatility, credit spreads, equities, and BTC begin deteriorating together; that transmission would turn a crypto unwind into a broader event.
